Definition: from G4253 and G2605; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise:--foretell, have notice, (shew) before.
BiblicalUsage: Prokatangello means to announce beforehand, to foretell, to promise. Peter says God showed before by the mouth of all his prophets that Christ should suffer, and Stephen says the prophets showed before of the coming of the Just One.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the prophets all spoke of one thing, and the suffering of Christ was announced long before it happened.
